entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Nandini Mishra,Ashish Kumar Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Ashish Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri R.P. Patel, learned A.G.A. for the State and also perused the record.
3.

The present application for anticipatory bail has been filed for protection in regard to FIR/Case Crime No. 419 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 of I.P.C., P.S.- Sihani Gate, District- Ghaziabad.
4. As per prosecution story, the named accused person Sameer Malik is stated to have purchased the land belonging to the defence estate from Majid.

The co-accused persons Om Pal and Neeraj Garg Ajay Veer vs State Of U.P. And Another on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44486132/
1 are stated to be the marginal witnesses of the said sale-deed.

entities.text: Neeraj Garg Ajay Veer vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said sale-deed has been executed for a consideration of Rs.10 crores.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case and has apprehension of his arrest.
He is a bonafide person and is a practising advocate at District Court Ghaziabad.
He is not named in the FIR and his name has come up later on in the statement of co-accused person which is not admissible in evidence.
Learned counsel has further stated that the applicant represented the seller Majid in the cases before the court concerned and had opened a joint account with him.
The applicant is not responsible for the money lying in the said joint account as it has been operated by co-accused Majid.
Learned counsel has also stated that the applicant as an Advocate had also moved an application u/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. on behalf of the co-accused Majid.
The applicant has no criminal history.
In case, his anticipatory bail application is allowed, he will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with the investigation/trial.

6. Per contra, learned AGA has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant on the ground that an amount of Rs.4.15 crores has been transferred to the account of the applicant and he is hand in glove with the main accused Majid.
Learned AGA has further stated that the applicant has misused the privilege granted by his profession and has maligned it.

7. After arguing at length, applicant's counsel has made a request that the present application for anticipatory bail may be disposed of with liberty to file a regular bail application which may be decided keeping in view the guidelines as laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, reported in 2022 SCC Online SC 825.
8.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, reported in 2022 SCC Online SC 825
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned A.G.A. has no objection to the prayer made by the learned counsel for the applicant.

9. After hearing learned counsel for the parties, no case is made out for interference u/s 438 Cr.P.C.
The present anticipatory bail application is disposed of with the direction that the applicant shall surrender before the court concerned within four weeks from today and in case, a regular bail application is filed, the same be decided in view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil (supra).
10.

For the period of four weeks from today or till the time of surrender of the applicant before the court concerned, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant, in the above case.
(Justice Krishan Pahal) Order Date :- 19.9.2023 Siddhant  Ajay Veer vs State Of U.P. And Another on 19 September, 2023
